# Kinematics vs dynamics

**Kinematics** is the geometry of motion: poses, joint angles, and how they relate. No mass, no force, no “will it actually get there.” FK and IK are kinematic. Setting `qpos` and running FK *teleports* the robot to that configuration.

**Dynamics** is Newton’s laws: given inertia, gravity, contact, and actuator forces, what acceleration happens next, then integrate. [`mj_step`](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/APIreference/APIfunctions.html#mj-step) / [`motrixsim.step`](https://motrixsim.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is dynamics (plus the FK needed to update poses). Mass, COM ([inertial frame](rotations-and-frames.qmd#link-frame-vs-inertial-frame)), and actuators matter here; they do not change FK. Simulator docs: [References — Robotics assets](references.qmd#robotics-assets).

| | Kinematics | Dynamics |
|---|---|---|
| Question | Where is it if `q` is this? | What happens if I apply these forces? |
| Inputs | `q` (and maybe `q̇` as geometry) | forces / `ctrl`, plus `q`, `q̇`, inertia |
| Typical call | FK, Jacobian, IK | `step`, inverse dynamics (`q̈` → `τ`) |
| Failure mode | Unreachable pose | Too weak, slips, tips, oscillates |

**Inverse dynamics** is not IK. IK: pose → `q`. Inverse dynamics: a desired `q̈` (or trajectory) → the torques that would produce it. Our `DampedIK` is the former.

Writing **controls** (`ctrl`) is the dynamic path: the integrator consumes them. Writing **state** (`qpos`) is kinematic: you skip the physics of getting there. The [state I/O](state-sensors-and-actuators.qmd#state-sensors-and-actuators) and [simulation loop](the-simulation-loop.qmd#the-simulation-loop) sections use that split.
